messages.content: Give an interview-style explanation of Sliding Window.
A sliding window maintains a range of elements while moving through a sequence. Many sliding-window algorithms run in O(n) time. It is useful for subarray sums and substring problems.
Explain the main idea behind Kadane Algorithm.
Kadane's algorithm finds the maximum-sum contiguous subarray in a one-dimensional array. It is useful for maximum subarray sum problems.
What should a beginner know about AVL Tree?
An AVL tree is a self-balancing binary search tree. Search, insertion, and deletion take O(log n).
Give a simple example of Segment Tree.
A segment tree can answer the sum of array elements from index 2 to index 5.
Explain Prefix Sum in simple words.
A prefix sum stores cumulative sums of array elements. It is useful for answering repeated range-sum queries.
When should we use Array?
Arrays are useful for storing ordered collections and performing index-based access.
What should a beginner know about Recursion?
Recursion solves a problem by calling a function on smaller instances of the same problem. Time and space complexity depend on the recurrence and recursion depth.
Explain the main idea behind Greedy Algorithm.
A greedy algorithm makes a locally optimal choice at each step. It is useful when a problem has the greedy-choice property and optimal substructure.
Explain the main idea behind Topological Sort.
Topological sorting orders the vertices of a directed acyclic graph so every edge goes from earlier to later. It is useful for course prerequisites and build dependencies.
What is Quick Sort?
Quicksort partitions elements around a pivot and recursively sorts the partitions.
What should a beginner know about BFS?
Breadth-First Search explores a graph level by level using a queue. With an adjacency list, BFS takes O(V + E) time.
Give an interview-style explanation of Fenwick Tree.
A Fenwick tree, also called a Binary Indexed Tree, maintains prefix aggregates efficiently. Updates and prefix queries take O(log n). It is useful for dynamic prefix sums and frequency counting.
Explain the main idea behind Sorting.
Sorting arranges elements according to a specified order. Sorting helps with searching, ranking, and duplicate detection.
Give an interview-style explanation of Tabulation.

Tabulation computes dynamic-programming states iteratively in dependency order. Its time complexity depends on the number of states and transitions. It is useful for bottom-up dynamic programming without recursive call overhead.
Explain the main idea behind Linked List.
A linked list consists of nodes that store data and links to other nodes. Linked lists are useful when frequent insertions and deletions are needed.
Give a simple example of Bit Manipulation.
For an integer x, x & 1 checks whether its least significant bit is set.
What is the time complexity associated with Disjoint Set Union?
With path compression and union by rank or size, operations are nearly O(1) amortized.
Give an interview-style explanation of Quick Sort.
Quicksort partitions elements around a pivot and recursively sorts the partitions. Its average time is O(n log n), while its worst case is O(n^2). It is useful for general-purpose in-memory sorting.
Give an interview-style explanation of Merge Sort.
Merge sort divides an array, sorts the parts, and merges them. Its time complexity is O(n log n), with O(n) auxiliary space for arrays. It is useful when predictable sorting performance is required.
Give an interview-style explanation of Hash Map.

A hash map stores key-value pairs using a hash function. Lookup, insertion, and deletion are O(1) on average and can degrade to O(n). Hash maps are useful for frequency counting, caching, and fast lookups.
Give an interview-style explanation of Linked List.

A linked list consists of nodes that store data and links to other nodes. Searching is O(n), and insertion at the head is O(1). Linked lists are useful when frequent insertions and deletions are needed.
What is Stack?
A stack follows LIFO, meaning Last In, First Out.
What is DFS?
Depth-First Search explores a path as far as possible before backtracking.
What should a beginner know about Greedy Algorithm?
A greedy algorithm makes a locally optimal choice at each step. Complexity depends on the choices and any sorting or data structures used.
Give a simple example of Hash Map.
A map can store the key 'apple' with the value 3.
Give an interview-style explanation of Memoization.

Memoization stores the results of previously solved recursive subproblems. It can reduce exponential recursive algorithms to polynomial time when there are only polynomially many states and transitions. It is useful for top-down dynamic programming.
Give a simple example of Hash Set.
Adding 5 twice still leaves only one copy of 5.
Give an interview-style explanation of Two Pointers.
The two-pointer technique uses two indices to process a collection efficiently. Many two-pointer algorithms run in O(n) time. It is useful for sorted pair-sum problems and removing duplicates.
What is the time complexity associated with Quick Sort?
Its average time is O(n log n), while its worst case is O(n^2).
Explain the main idea behind Heap.
A heap is a complete binary tree that satisfies a heap-order property. Heaps are useful for priority queues and top-k problems.
Give a simple example of Recursion.
Factorial satisfies factorial(n) = n * factorial(n - 1), with a base case at zero.
Give a simple example of Linked List.
A list can contain nodes 10 -> 20 -> 30.
Explain Binary Search in simple words.
Binary search repeatedly halves a sorted search interval. It is useful for searching sorted data and finding monotonic boundaries.
Give an interview-style explanation of Segment Tree.

A segment tree stores information about array intervals in a tree structure. Building takes O(n), while typical point updates and range queries take O(log n). It is useful for range-sum, minimum, maximum, and other associative range queries.
